blocks.source: Vol IV, Trajectory Planning, § Historical Perspective and Further Reading
blocks.md: Motion planning became a concrete computational discipline when @lozanoperez1983spatial mapped geometric collision avoidance into configuration-space search, shrinking the geometry of a complex moving body to a single point. In the same year, @schwartz1983piano formulated the piano movers' problem through exact algebraic decomposition. While theoretically complete, exact algebraic methods scale doubly exponentially with degrees of freedom, rendering them intractable for multi-joint manipulators. In the 1990s, randomized sampling bypassed this geometric bottleneck by trading exact completeness for probabilistic guarantees.

questions.q: The section **Historical Perspective and Further Reading** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A collision-free path is executable only if every joint's position, velocity, acceleration, jerk, torque, and current stay within limits along the continuous interpolant, its seams, and its stop, which time parameterization must check.

Receding-horizon MPC handles constraints explicitly and gains recursive feasibility only through a terminal invariant set, and its solve time against the period decides whether its output can be admitted.
Phase-plane time parameterization finds the fastest timing of a fixed path under velocity, acceleration, and torque bounds, and online generators compute jerk-limited profiles from arbitrary states.
A differential-drive base reaches the same configurations as a holonomic one but through a restricted velocity space, so it plans over controls.
